cards.headline: Boy taken to hospital after signboard collapses at foodcourt in Rivervale Mall
bullets: A boy was sent to hospital after a signboard fell at a foodcourt in Rivervale Mall.
The incident happened at a Food Junction outlet on June 20.
The boy is now recovering at home.
Food Junction has checked safety measures and reopened the outlet.

cards.headline: Disney Dessert Besties at Pasir Ris Mall, Drone Soccer Try-outs at Chinatown Point
bullets: Disney plushies are on sale at Pasir Ris Mall until June 28.
You can buy a Disney plushie for $19 or a set of four for $65.
Chinatown Point has free game stations with remote-controlled cars until June 28.
Try drone soccer at Chinatown Point from June 29 to July 5.
Spend $40 at Chinatown Point and its sister malls for rewards and a lucky draw.

cards.headline: Men should step up when it comes to sharing household responsibilities
bullets: Women do three times more care and housework than men globally.
Singapore offers 30 weeks of shared parental leave for new parents.
Many couples believe household chores are shared, but women still do more.
Family planning is often seen as a woman's issue, with men taking a passive role.

cards.headline: How greater transparency puts pressure on property agents and agencies to do better
bullets: Consumers can now easily check property agents' past disciplinary actions for the last three years.
This makes it harder for agents with bad records to get business.
Complaints against agents rose 13% last year, with poor service and misleading ads being common issues.
A major property agency was censured for the first time for its agents' misleading ads.

cards.headline: Mass-mating of corals in Singapore muted in 2026, may reflect lower resilience across reef
bullets: Singapore corals had a quiet mass-mating season in April and May 2026.
This could mean the reefs are less healthy overall, scientists say.
Past marine heatwaves and bleaching events likely weakened the corals.
Some coral types, like the moon coral, still managed to reproduce.
More research is needed to understand the impact on reef recovery.

cards.headline: Nmixx Episode 1 Zero Frontier concert in Singapore: K-pop sextet dazzles with powerhouse vocals and heartfelt chemistry
bullets: K-pop group Nmixx held their first world tour concert in Singapore on Saturday at The Star Theatre.
The sextet impressed with powerful live vocals and a live band, including a saxophonist.
Member Lily was a standout with her strong singing and humorous interactions with the crowd.
Sullyoon performed despite a back injury, singing most of the show while seated.
The concert highlighted Nmixx's strong vocals and close bond between the group members.

cards.headline: Two men arrested after allegedly swapping diamond worth over S$235,000 with fake at a store
bullets: The suspects were arrested at Changi Airport Terminal 3 within three hours of the report being made, with the stolen diamond recovered and seized.
See the article for full details.

cards.headline: Harbourfront Centre to cease operations on Jul 27
bullets: Harbourfront Centre will close its doors for good on July 27.
The Singapore Cruise Centre is moving to a new spot nearby from July 15.
The mall will be torn down and rebuilt as a new 33-storey building.
It was first opened in 1978 as the World Trade Centre.

cards.headline: These stay-at-home dads started a workshop to help fathers style their daughters' hair
bullets: Two stay-at-home dads started a workshop called Dads and Braids.
Fathers learn how to style their daughters' hair in the workshop.
The sessions aim to build confidence and challenge caregiving stereotypes.
The idea came about after the founders struggled with their own daughters' hair.

cards.headline: Fire breaks out at Whampoa hawker centre, 100 people evacuated
bullets: A fire at Whampoa Makan Place involved a stall's kitchen exhaust ducting.
About 100 people were evacuated from the hawker centre as a precaution.
The fire started around 4.10pm and was put out by the SCDF.
No injuries were reported from the incident.
Hawkers returned to check their stalls after the cordon was removed.

cards.headline: 2026 XPeng X9 Pro review: After four days, the range was a surprise
bullets: The new XPeng X9 Pro electric car is as long as a Rolls-Royce but can park itself.
It has a huge boot space even with all seven seats up.
The car offers luxury features like a flip-down cinema screen and massage seats.
Its electric range is about 740 km, more than advertised.
The driver's seat is not its best feature for sporty driving.

cards.headline: US mortgage rates fall to lowest in month as Middle East tensions ease
bullets: US home loan rates dropped to the lowest in a month.
The average 30-year fixed loan rate fell to 6.47%.
Easing Middle East tensions helped lower inflation worries.
Homebuyer relief comes as the spring selling season ends.

cards.headline: Spain lacks 750,000 homes, with hot spots from Madrid to the Mediterranean coast
bullets: Spain is short 750,000 homes, with the problem worse in big cities and coastal areas.
This housing shortage is driven by more people forming households than new homes being built.
Home prices rose nearly 10% last year, making it harder for people to buy.
Younger people are finding it tougher to own homes or live independently.
Rents are also going up, with many tenants spending over 40% of their income on housing.

cards.headline: Perhaps Fifa was right about the World Cup ticket pricing after all
bullets: World Cup ticket prices shot up by 23% just days before games.
Even matches between less popular teams saw resale tickets costing over US$400.
Fifa's pricing system is making them record profits, despite criticism.
Stadiums are mostly full, and TV ratings are breaking records.
The expanded World Cup format with 48 teams is proving popular.

cards.headline: Pimco targets out-of-date assets in new real estate strategy
bullets: Pimco will buy old buildings and fix them up to be greener and more attractive.
The company is looking for older properties in good spots that can be updated.
They want to make buildings better suited for a world with more extreme weather.
Pimco will avoid areas where climate change makes insurance hard to get.

cards.headline: S'pore national badminton player Yeo Jia Min marries ex-national swimmer Pang Sheng Jun
bullets: Badminton player Yeo Jia Min married ex-swimmer Pang Sheng Jun on June 20.
The couple had a church wedding ceremony in Tampines.
They got engaged last December.
Several local celebrities and athletes attended the wedding.

cards.headline: Boy in China, 12, steals neighbour's car for joyride, claims he's adult with dwarfism when caught
bullets: A 12-year-old boy in China stole a neighbour's car and drove for over six hours.
He was caught after running out of money for the highway toll.
The boy lied to police, claiming he was a 22-year-old adult with dwarfism.
He learned to drive in secret and took the car without his father's knowledge.
Police gave him a warning as he is under 14 and ordered his parents to discipline him.

cards.headline: 'Not a hero, I just did what I had to do': M'sian man uses lorry to stop runaway bus, gets hailed a hero
bullets: A Malaysian lorry driver stopped a runaway bus with his vehicle on an expressway.
He said he was not a hero, just doing what was necessary.
The incident happened on June 16 on the North-South Expressway.
Dashcam footage showed the bus speeding and narrowly missing cars.

cards.headline: This New Inclusive Playground In Tampines Has Wheelchair-Friendly Equipment & Low-Sensory Zones
bullets: A new inclusive playground with wheelchair-friendly swings and low-sensory zones has opened in Tampines.
The playground at Sun Plaza Park allows children of all abilities to play together.
It features barrier-free access, special slides, and quiet 'Hideaway Huts'.
A sensory garden and colourful design help with visibility and navigation for all.

cards.headline: The Clifford Pier Was Once Singapore’s Main Arrival Point By Sea & Home To New Year’s Day Races
bullets: Clifford Pier was Singapore's main arrival point for immigrants and cargo.
It was also known as Ang Teng Beh Tau or Red Lamp Pier.
The pier hosted the Annual New Year's Day Sea Sports Regatta.
It was named after Sir Hugh Clifford, Governor of the Straits Settlements.

cards.headline: First Look At Cj Hendry’s Juju World – Giant Inflatables, SG-Exclusive Merch & What To Expect
bullets: Artist Cj Hendry's new exhibition 'juju world' features giant yellow inflatables and exclusive merchandise.
Singapore is the only place in the world where the 'juju' character will be yellow.
You can buy small collectible 'juju' figures in blind boxes for $39 each.
The exhibition includes a large ball pit filled with mini 'juju' characters and inflatable slides.
Visitors need to wear socks and sign a waiver before entering the exhibition.
